How to Negate in Arabic

Arabic has several ways to say "not" depending on context—notably, on the tense of a sentence. Here's a list of the most basic patterns.

To negate the present tense, you typically use لا (lā). For example: لا يتكلم (lā yatakallamu) = "He doesn't talk" or "He isn't talking."

In Classical Arabic, جاء ب (jā'a bi) means literally "he came with (something)". That can often be translated as "he brought". For example, جاء بالكتاب (jā'a bi-l-kitāb) = "He came with the book" or "He brought the book."

In several dialects, the phrase جاء ب (jā'a bi) has been reanalysed as a verb
